meta.mapLabel: Dependency map of the Goldbach-gap results. Arrows point from a result to what it relies on.
intro: Unless a box says otherwise, ‘the record’ is the budget game: the largest g(N) for N below 10^200 (standing: 160,357). The research also plays a height game (N unbounded; 10,000,141) and a threshold game (smallest N with g above 100,000; 150 digits).
Each box is one result: a Lean theorem checked by the kernel, a research finding, a search result or a record. Arrows point from a result to what it relies on.
Tap a box for a plain-words summary, what it means for the record, and where it lives. Tap an arrow to see why that link matters.
Boxes are coloured by role. Switch the lens to colour by evidence (how solid the result is), by impact (what it does for the record chase) or by what is new since the 23 Nov map.
Solid arrows: the proof text names the other result. Dashed: a chain of references. Dotted: a document states the link.

meta.newsTitle: What changed since the map of 23 Nov
news: New record: 160,357 (24 Nov, 17:11 UTC, 7.53% of the ceiling), proved in the kernel 38 minutes after the find. How it was found: ; its theorem: .

A theory of cover depth, the biggest addition: how far n moduli can strike the primes with no luck. Lean defines it (), proves it exactly for up to nine moduli, certifies covers up to 614,101 on 1,228 moduli and counts them (). Exhaustive searches give and .
The law for the number of covers and its derivation (, ), the limit 1.1275 it first gave, a referee's check of it and its withdrawal the next morning (, , ); Lean proves the exact first steps ().
Why 1.349 is not the truth: , with , and (my own, written for the research session and not checked by anyone).

No limit of the cover depth is known now. The research session withdrew 1.1275 itself (the small moduli do not have the entropy the recursion gave them: ) and then its replacement, after the Lean session found , which gives a rigorous depth of order r ln² r·ln₃ r/(ln₂ r)² (written out by me); see also and , whose verdict that the ratio tends to 0 I withdrew. Nothing changes at the campaign's sizes.

In the kernel, the same day: and (the factor ln₃ of the paper bound is the only thing left on paper), and : 347 digits for a gap above 200,000, certified, and 2,196 digits for a million (certificate in progress).

Is it new? A literature check (note LITERATURE_SEARCH.md): nothing earlier than 2026 was found on lower bounds for the least Goldbach summand; Shi (2026) has half of ln X ln ln X; Radomskii (Nov 2026, unrefereed) probably implies ln X·(ln ln X)², so our two bounds are probably not new as statements if his lemma holds, while their Lean proofs are independent of it.

Seven mechanisms outside the closure grammar were scored on the exact miniature, out of sample (): anything computed from the small-prime residues is worth at most 0.1 nats, size of N 0.1 to 0.3, and one mechanism, , reaches 1.4 nats when verification is free, goes to between −0.8 and +0.2 when it is priced, and is bounded at +0.035 nats at the campaign's cover (research session's computation).

The bottom-up round (the user's instruction to discover new mathematics or build from the bottom up): finds nothing that lowers the 36.46 nats (exponent 78.3, then 52.2, then 36.46, then the window of 16.9 nats; a pin beyond 463 pays what the cover pays), and a model of the success chance reproduces the 69 published records of the least Goldbach summand (+0.06 ± 0.34 nats for N ≥ 8·10¹³). Two earlier answers now have boxes: (seven candidates in the arithmetic of the rows, the prime-gap toolbox, the covering theorems) and (0.36 of the agreement it needs).
Door 1 is measured: ; the final record depends on ; .
The fleet: ; and raised the rate.
A second game, a fixed gap with the fewest digits, is priced (, ) and has a first cover ().
In Lean: a generator for A025018 proved correct (, ), Goldbach and the record holders below 2^25 by a kernel-run sieve (), and finding covers for arbitrary rows shown as hard as SAT ().
Correction to the first map: the primality chains are 26 steps for 158,209 and 21 for 160,357, not 27. Switch the lens to New to see every new (red) and changed (ochre) box.

nodes.title: Definition: least Goldbach summand g(N)
nodes.gist: p is a Goldbach summand of N if both p and N − p are prime. g(N) is the least such p. Every record in the project is a statement about how large g(N) can be.
nodes.detail: In the library: IsSummand N p and IsLeastSummand N s. Everything else on the map is about proving, bounding or certifying statements of this form.
nodes.source:
/-- `s` is the least Goldbach summand of `N`, the paper's `g(N) = s`. -/
def IsLeastSummand (N s : ℕ) : Prop := IsSummand N s ∧ ∀ p, IsSummand N p → s ≤ p

nodes.title: Primorial core: multiples of 2·3·5···P are deserts
nodes.gist: If N is a multiple of the product of all primes up to P (and N > 2P), then no prime up to P is a Goldbach summand of N.
nodes.detail: Each small prime p divides N and itself, so it divides N − p, making N − p composite. This is the simplest possible cover: every prime covers only itself. It forces N to be astronomically large (about e^P), which is why cleverer covers matter.
nodes.source:
/-- Paper Lemma `lem:primcore` (primorial core): if the primorial of `P` divides `N`
and `N > 2P`, then no prime `≤ P` is a Goldbach summand of `N`. -/
theorem not_isSummand_of_primorial_dvd {N P p : ℕ} (hN : primorial P ∣ N) (hbig : 2 * P < N)
    (hpP : p ≤ P) : ¬ IsSummand N p := by
  rintro ⟨hp, hq⟩
  have hpN : p ∣ N := (hp.dvd_primorial_iff.mpr hpP).trans hN
  have hdiv : p ∣ N - p := Nat.dvd_sub hpN dvd_rfl
  have heq : p = N - p := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hp hq).mp hdiv
  have := hq.two_le
  omega

note.text: The idea the whole project starts from. The covering trick keeps the effect and shrinks N.

nodes.title: Every odd prime is a least summand
nodes.gist: For every odd prime s there are arbitrarily large even N with g(N) = s.
nodes.detail: Dirichlet's theorem gives a prime t ≡ −s modulo the primorial of s − 1, and N = s + t works. Sharp form of paper Theorem thm:dirichlet.
nodes.source:
/-- Paper Theorem `thm:dirichlet`, in its sharp form: every odd prime `s` is the least
Goldbach summand of arbitrarily large even numbers. The proof is the paper's:
Dirichlet's theorem gives a prime `t ≡ -s` modulo the primorial of `s - 1`,
and `N = s + t` works. -/
theorem exists_isLeastSummand {s : ℕ} (hs : s.Prime) (hs2 : s ≠ 2) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ N > n, Even N ∧ IsLeastSummand N s := by
  have hs3 : 3 ≤ s := by
    have := hs.two_le
    omega
  set M := primorial (s - 1) with hM
  have hM0 : M ≠ 0 := primorial_ne_zero _
  have : NeZero M := ⟨hM0⟩
  have hcop : s.Coprime M := by
    rw [hs.coprime_iff_not_dvd, hM, hs.dvd_primorial_iff]
    omega
  have hunit : IsUnit (-(s : ZMod M)) := ((ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime s M).mpr hcop).neg
  obtain ⟨t, htbig, ht, htmod⟩ := Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod hunit (n + s)
  have hMN : M ∣ s + t := by
    rw [← ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff]
    push_cast
    rw [htmod]
    ring
  have h2M : 2 ∣ M := by
    rw [hM, Nat.prime_two.dvd_primorial_iff]
...

note.text: Qualitative: shows what values occur but says nothing about how large N must be.

nodes.title: g(N) is unbounded
nodes.gist: For every bound B there is an even N, with a Goldbach partition, all of whose Goldbach summands exceed B.
nodes.detail: A one-line consequence of the previous theorem.
nodes.source:
/-- The least Goldbach summand is unbounded: for every bound `B` there is an even `N`
that has a Goldbach partition, all of whose Goldbach summands exceed `B`. -/
theorem least_summand_unbounded (B : ℕ) :
    ∃ N s, Even N ∧ IsLeastSummand N s ∧ B < s := by
  obtain ⟨s, hsB, hs⟩ := Nat.exists_infinite_primes (B + 3)
  obtain ⟨N, -, hNeven, hN⟩ := exists_isLeastSummand hs (by omega) 0
  exact ⟨N, s, hNeven, hN, by omega⟩

nodes.title: Effective size of N, assuming Linnik
nodes.gist: Assuming Linnik's theorem on the least prime in a progression, every odd prime s is the least summand of some even N ≤ C·(primorial(s−1))^L + s, which gives g(N) ≥ c·log N for these N.
nodes.detail: The hypothesis is stated as a named assumption (LinnikStatement). The bound c·log N is far weaker than the covering bound below.
nodes.source:
/-- **Effective form of paper Theorem `thm:dirichlet`.** Under Linnik's theorem, with its
constants `C`, `L`: every odd prime `s` is the least Goldbach summand of an even
`N ≤ C · (primorial (s - 1))^L + s`. -/
theorem exists_isLeastSummand_le_of_linnik (h : LinnikStatement) :
    ∃ C L : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < L ∧ ∀ s : ℕ, s.Prime → s ≠ 2 →
      ∃ N : ℕ, Even N ∧ IsLeastSummand N s ∧
        (N : ℝ) ≤ C * (primorial (s - 1) : ℝ) ^ L + s := by

nodes.title: Covering certificate
nodes.gist: If every odd prime q below Q lies in a residue class a mod some modulus r, and N is in all these classes, then each N − q is divisible by that r. So no prime below Q is a Goldbach summand of N.
nodes.detail: The central trick of the project. Choosing the classes (the cover) is a design problem; finding N is then a Chinese-remainder step. The moduli need not even be prime for this direction.
nodes.source:
theorem not_isSummand_of_cover {R : Finset ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} {N Q : ℕ}
    (hR : ∀ r ∈ R, 2 ≤ r)
    (hcover : ∀ q, q.Prime → q ≠ 2 → q < Q → ∃ r ∈ R, q ≡ a r [MOD r])
    (hN : ∀ r ∈ R, N ≡ a r [MOD r]) (heven : Even N)
    (hbig : ∀ r ∈ R, Q + r < N) (hbig2 : Q + 2 < N)
    {q : ℕ} (hqQ : q < Q) : ¬ IsSummand N q := by
  rintro ⟨hq, hNq⟩
  by_cases hq2 : q = 2
  · subst hq2
    have h2 : 2 ∣ N - 2 := Nat.dvd_sub (even_iff_two_dvd.mp heven) dvd_rfl
    have := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq Nat.prime_two hNq).mp h2
    omega
  · obtain ⟨r, hr, hqr⟩ := hcover q hq hq2 hqQ
    have hle : q ≤ N := by
      have := hbig r hr
      omega
    have hdvd : r ∣ N - q := (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd' hle).mp (hqr.trans (hN r hr).symm)
    rcases (Nat.dvd_prime hNq).mp hdvd with h1 | h1
    · have := hR r hr
      omega
    · have := hbig r hr
      omega

note.text: Every record on the map is this theorem plus work to choose a good cover and extend it by luck.

nodes.title: Every cover is realised by some N
nodes.gist: For any cover by classes modulo distinct odd primes there are arbitrarily large even N in all the classes that do have a Goldbach partition, and their least summand is at least Q.
nodes.detail: Uses Dirichlet's theorem twice. It proves existence only; it gives no bound on the size of N. That missing bound is exactly what the capped game adds.
nodes.source:
/-- Paper Theorem `thm:coverdirichlet` (unconditional realisation). Any covering of the
odd primes below `Q` by classes modulo distinct odd primes is realised by arbitrarily
large even numbers `N` that have a Goldbach partition; for each of them the least
Goldbach summand `g` exists and satisfies `Q ≤ g`. The proof applies Dirichlet's theorem
twice, as in the paper. -/
theorem exists_isLeastSummand_of_cover {R : Finset ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} {Q : ℕ}

    (hcover : ∀ q, q.Prime → q ≠ 2 → q < Q → ∃ r ∈ R, q ≡ a r [MOD r]) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ N > n, Even N ∧ (∀ r ∈ R, N ≡ a r [MOD r]) ∧ ∃ g, IsLeastSummand N g ∧ Q ≤ g := by
  classical
  have hr3 : ∀ r ∈ R, 3 ≤ r := fun r hr => by
    have h1 := (hR r hr).1.two_le
    have h2 := (hR r hr).2
    omega
  set M := ∏ r ∈ R, r with hM
  have hM0 : M ≠ 0 := Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr fun r hr => by
    have := hr3 r hr
    omega
  have hrM : ∀ r ∈ R, r ∣ M := fun r hr => Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem (fun r => r) hr

nodes.title: Mertens' first theorem
nodes.gist: For all N ≥ 1, |Σ Λ(n)/n − ln N| ≤ 6, the sum over n ≤ N of the von Mangoldt function over n.
nodes.detail: The base of the Mertens chain in this library.
nodes.source:
/-- **Mertens' first theorem** at the integers: `|∑_{n ≤ N} Λ(n)/n - ln N| ≤ 6`. -/
theorem abs_sum_lam_sub_log_le (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    |∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n / n - Real.log N| ≤ 6 := by
  have hNpos : (0 : ℝ) < N := by exact_mod_cast hN
  have key : ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n * ((N / n : ℕ) : ℝ) = ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Real.log n := by
    rw [← ArithmeticFunction.sum_Ioc_mul_zeta_eq_sum, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_mul_zeta]
    simp [ArithmeticFunction.log_apply]
  have hup : ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n * ((N / n : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ N * ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n / n := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun n hn => ?_
    calc Λ n * ((N / n : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ Λ n * ((N : ℝ) / n) :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left Nat.cast_div_le ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_nonneg
      _ = N * (Λ n / n) := by ring
  have hlow : N * ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n / n - ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n
      ≤ ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, Λ n * ((N / n : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun n

nodes.title: Mertens' third theorem
nodes.gist: ln w · ∏ over primes p ≤ w of (1 − 1/p) tends to e^(−γ).
nodes.detail: Proved from Mathlib in Mertens.lean (the library's own note says it is not in Mathlib). It is the one analytic fact that gives the sharp constant e^γ/(2C₂) in the covering bound.
nodes.source:
/-- **Mertens' third theorem**: `ln w · ∏_{p ≤ w} (1 - 1/p) → e^{-γ}`. -/
theorem mertens_third :
    Tendsto (fun w : ℕ => Real.log w * ∏ p ∈ Nat.primesLE w, (1 - (p : ℝ)⁻¹)) atTop
      (𝓝 (Real.exp (-Real.eulerMascheroniConstant))) := by
  have h := (Real.continuous_exp.tendsto _).comp tendsto_log_log_add_sum
  refine h.congr' ?_
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 3] with w hw
  have hw3 : (3 : ℝ) ≤ w := by exact_mod_cast hw
  have hlw : 0 < Real.log w := Real.log_pos (by linarith)
  simp only [Function.comp_apply]
  rw [Real.exp_add, Real.exp_log hlw, Real.exp_sum]
  congr 1
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun p hp => ?_
  have hpp := (Nat.mem_primesLE.mp hp).2
  have hp2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ p := by exact_mod_cast hpp.two_le
  have hx : (p : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ 1 / 2 := by
    rw [inv_eq_one_div]
    exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by norm_num) hp2
  exact Real.exp_log (by linarith)

note.text: Where the constant 1.349 comes from. Pure asymptotics: it does not help choose a cover for 10^200.

nodes.title: Prime number theorem as two inequalities
nodes.gist: For every δ > 0 and large x, (1 − δ)·x/ln x ≤ π(x) ≤ (1 + δ)·x/ln x.
nodes.detail: Stated in the form the covering bound needs. No hypothesis in the Lean statement.
nodes.source:
/-- The prime number theorem as two inequalities: for every `δ > 0` and all large `x`,
`(1 - δ) x / ln x ≤ π(x) ≤ (1 + δ) x / ln x`. -/
theorem eventually_primeCounting_bounds {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, (1 - δ) * (x / Real.log x) ≤ (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) ∧

nodes.title: Elementary Mertens-type upper bound (κ = 1.367)
nodes.gist: The product over odd primes r ≤ w of (r − 2)/(r − 1) is at most about 1.367 / ln w, proved without Mertens' third theorem.
nodes.detail: Enough for an unconditional covering bound with constant 0.73.
nodes.source:
/-- The elementary instance of `MertensUpper`, with `κ = 1575/1152 = 1.367`. -/
theorem mertensUpper_elementary : MertensUpper (1575 / 1152) := by
  intro ε hε
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 7] with w hw
  have hw7 : (7 : ℝ) ≤ w := by exact_mod_cast hw
  have hlog : 0 < Real.log (w : ℝ) := Real.log_pos (by linarith)
  have hle : Real.log (w : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((w : ℝ) + 1) :=
    Real.log_le_log (by linarith) (by linarith)
  calc oddPrimeProd w ≤ 1575 / 1152 / Real.log (w + 1) := oddPrimeProd_le hw
    _ ≤ 1575 / 1152 / Real.log w := div_le_div_of_nonneg_left (by norm_num) hlog hle
    _ ≤ (1575 / 1152 + ε) / Real.log w := by
        apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hlog.le
        linarith

nodes.title: Covering bound, unconditional: c = 0.73
nodes.gist: For all large X there is an even N ≤ X such that N − q is composite for every prime q < 0.73·ln X·ln ln X.
nodes.detail: Uses only the elementary Mertens-type bound. The constant 1152/1575 = 0.7314… is rounded down. Covering beats counting here: counting gives at best 1/2. Since 24 Nov it is built from the cover stated in depth form.
nodes.source:
/-- **Unconditional.** For all large `X` there is an even `N ≤ X` (above the threshold) such
that `N - q` is composite for every prime `q < 0.73 · ln X · ln ln X`. The constant is
`1152/1575 = 0.7314…` rounded down; counting pairs of primes gives `1/2` and no more. -/
theorem eventually_exists_even_le_no_summand :
    ∀ᶠ X : ℕ in atTop, ∃ N : ℕ, 0.73 * Real.log X * Real.log (Real.log X) < N ∧ N ≤ X ∧ Even N ∧
      ∀ q : ℕ, (q : ℝ) < 0.73 * Real.log X * Real.log (Real.log X) → ¬ IsSummand N q :=
  eventually_exists_even_le_of_mertensUpper (by norm_num) mertensUpper_elementary (by norm_num)

nodes.title: Covering bound with explicit constant c = 1.2
nodes.gist: For all large X there is an even N ≤ X such that N − q is composite for every prime q < 1.2·ln X·ln ln X.
nodes.detail: Uses the crude numerical bounds on γ and C₂ plus Mertens' third theorem. The limit of the method is 1.349.
nodes.source:
/-- **An explicit constant, with no hypothesis.** For all large `X` there is an even `N ≤ X`
such that `N - q` is composite for every prime `q < 1.2 · ln X · ln ln X`. (The crude bounds
`γ > 1/2` and `C₂ ≤ 0.684` are used; the limit of the method is `1.349`.) -/
theorem eventually_exists_even_le_no_summand_six_fifths :
    ∀ᶠ X : ℕ in atTop, ∃ N : ℕ, 1.2 * Real.log X * Real.log (Real.log X) < N ∧ N ≤ X ∧ Even N ∧
      ∀ q : ℕ, (q : ℝ) < 1.2 * Real.log X * Real.log (Real.log X) → ¬ IsSummand N q :=
  eventually_exists_even_le_of_mertensThird_explicit mertensThird

nodes.title: Covering bound, sharp: c < e^γ/(2C₂) = 1.349…
nodes.gist: For every c below e^γ/(2·C₂) = 1.349… and all large X there is an even N ≤ X such that N − q is composite for every prime q < c·ln X·ln ln X. No hypothesis.
nodes.detail: Rests on the layered covering lemma, the prime number theorem and Mertens' third theorem. Also proved in the version that assumes Mertens as a hypothesis, as first written. At X = 10^200 the formula gives about 3,800, which is only for scale: 'large X' is not explicit in the theorem. Since 24 Nov the file also states the cover itself, in depth form, as its own theorem; this one is built from it.
nodes.source:
/-- **The covering bound with the sharp constant, with no hypothesis.** If
`c · 2 C₂ e^{-γ} < 1`, that is `c < e^γ / (2 C₂) = 1.349…` (`C₂` the twin-prime constant, `γ`
Euler's constant), then for all large `X` there is an even `N ≤ X` such that `N - q` is
composite for every prime `q < c · ln X · ln ln X`. -/
theorem eventually_exists_even_le_of_mul_lt_one {c : ℝ}
    (hc : c * (2 * twinPrimeConstant * Real.exp (-Real.eulerMascheroniConstant)) < 1) :
    ∀ᶠ X : ℕ in atTop, ∃ N : ℕ, c * Real.log X * Real.log (Real.log X) < N ∧ N ≤ X ∧ Even N ∧
      ∀ q : ℕ, (q : ℝ) < c * Real.log X * Real.log (Real.log X) → ¬ IsSummand N q :=
  eventually_exists_even_le_of_mertensThird mertensThird hc

note.text: The record 160,357 is about 42 times larger than what this asymptotic formula would suggest at 10^200. Theory is a floor, not a guide; the records come from the capped-game design.  Superseded on 25 Nov: formally in the kernel for every constant and in the order ln X·(ln ln X)²/(150000 (ln ln ln X)²) (boxes ‘The covering bound for every constant, in the kernel’ and ‘The order of the covering bound in the kernel’).

nodes.title: Prime moduli suffice
nodes.gist: A cover built from composite moduli, prime powers or overlapping classes can always be replaced by one using prime moduli that kills at least the same rows.
nodes.detail: Justifies restricting attention to prime moduli, as the records do (the odd primes 3 to 463): composite or prime-power moduli cannot do better.
nodes.source:
/-- **Prime moduli suffice.** Given any family of congruence conditions `x ≡ a i (mod m i)`
with moduli `m i ≥ 2` (composite, prime powers, with common factors: anything), there are
primes `r i ∣ m i` such that every `N` in all the classes modulo the `m i` is in all the
classes modulo the `r i`, and every row killed through `m i` is killed through `r i`. -/
theorem prime_moduli_suffice {ι : Type*} (m a : ι → ℕ) (hm : ∀ i, 2 ≤ m i) :
    ∃ r : ι → ℕ, (∀ i, (r i).Prime ∧ r i ∣ m i) ∧
      (∀ N, (∀ i, N ≡ a i [MOD m i]) → ∀ i, N ≡ a i [MOD r i]) ∧
      ∀ q i, q ≡ a i [MOD m i] → q ≡ a i [MOD r i] := by
  refine ⟨fun i => (m i).minFac, fun i => ⟨Nat.minFac_prime ?_, Nat.minFac_dvd _⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have := hm i
    omega
  · intro N hN i
    exact (hN i).of_dvd (Nat.minFac_dvd _)
  · intro q i h
    exact h.of_dvd (Nat.minFac_dvd _)

nodes.title: Kills are residues
nodes.gist: For q + 2 ≤ N, the number N − q is composite exactly when q ≡ N modulo some prime r whose square is at most N − q.
nodes.detail: The exact bookkeeping of the game: a row N − q is killed by the prime r precisely when q lies in N's residue class modulo r. All the counting laws below are built on it.
nodes.source:
/-- **Kills are residues.** For `q + 2 ≤ N`, the row `N - q` is composite exactly when
`q ≡ N` modulo some prime `r` with `r² ≤ N - q`. -/
theorem not_prime_sub_iff {N q : ℕ} (h : q + 2 ≤ N) :
    ¬ (N - q).Prime ↔ ∃ r, r.Prime ∧ r * r ≤ N - q ∧ q ≡ N [MOD r] := by
  have hle : q ≤ N := by omega
  constructor
  · intro hnp
    refine ⟨(N - q).minFac, Nat.minFac_prime (by omega), ?_, ?_⟩
    · have := Nat.minFac_sq_le_self (by omega : 0 < N - q) hnp
      rwa [sq] at this
    · exact (dvd_sub_iff hle).mp (Nat.minFac_dvd _)
  · rintro ⟨r, hr, hsq, hmod⟩ hp
    have hdvd : r ∣ N - q := (dvd_sub_iff hle).mpr hmod
    have hreq : r = N - q := (Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq hr hp).mp hdvd
    have h2 := hr.two_le
    rw [← hreq] at hsq
    have : r * 2 ≤ r * r := Nat.mul_le_mul_left r h2
    omega

nodes.title: Two rows share only small divisors
nodes.gist: A common divisor of two different rows N − q and N − q′ (both below the row bound Q) is itself below Q. So any number r ≥ Q divides at most one row.
nodes.detail: A large modulus can therefore kill at most one row. This is the root of the 'above Q no list pays' limit further down. The same file also records that a prime at or above Q divides at most one row (row_unique_of_le).
nodes.source:
/-- **Two rows share only small divisors**: a common divisor of two different rows below `Q`
is itself below `Q`. -/
theorem lt_of_dvd_two_rows {N q q' r Q : ℕ} (hq' : q' ≤ N) (hlt : q < q') (hQ : q' < Q)
    (h : r ∣ N - q) (h' : r ∣ N - q') : r < Q := by
  have hd := dvd_sub_rows hq' hlt h h'
  have := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hd
  omega

nodes.title: Budget law: the cap limits how many designs fit
nodes.gist: For pairwise coprime moduli with allowed-residue sets A_r, the number of N below X that meet every allowed set is at most (∏|A_r|)·(X/∏r + 1).
nodes.detail: The exact accounting of the cap. N lives in a progression modulo the product of the moduli, so each extra modulus shrinks the room. With the 89 odd primes up to 463 the product is about 10^192, which leaves about 2×10^7 even numbers below 10^200 per choice of residues. Adding 467 and 479 would leave about 95.
nodes.source:
/-- **The budget law with choice sets.** Let `S` be pairwise coprime positive moduli and let
`A r` be the set of residues allowed modulo `r`. The number of `N < X` whose residue modulo
every `r ∈ S` is allowed is at most `(∏ |A r|) · (X / ∏ r + 1)`. -/
theorem card_residues_in_le (S : Finset ℕ) (A : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ)
    (hpos : ∀ r ∈ S, 0 < r) (hcop : (S : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime) :
    #{N ∈ range X | ∀ r ∈ S, N % r ∈ A r} ≤ (∏ r ∈ S, #(A r)) * (X / (∏ r ∈ S, r) + 1) := by
  classical
  set M := ∏ r ∈ S, r with hM
  have hM0 : 0 < M := Finset.prod_pos hpos
  rw [← Finset.card_pi, ← Finset.card_range (X / M + 1), ← Finset.card_product]
  refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun N => (fun r _ => N % r, N / M)) ?_ ?_
  · intro N hN
    rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range] at hN
    rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_pi, Finset.mem_range]
    exact ⟨fun r hr => hN.2 r hr, Nat.lt_succ_of_le (Nat.div_le_div_right hN.1.le)⟩
  · intro N _ N' _ heq

note.text: Shows the trade-off behind using moduli up to 463: more moduli kill more rows but leave fewer candidates to search.

nodes.title: First moment: an average design exists
nodes.gist: Summed over all non-zero residue vectors, the number of rows left alive is exactly |P|·∏(r − 2). So some vector leaves at most |P|·∏(r − 2)/∏(r − 1) rows.
nodes.detail: The existence engine for covers: pigeonhole on an exact identity. The exact sum is sum_card_rowsLeft; the averaged bound is exists_rowsLeft_le.
nodes.source:
/-- **Pigeonhole for covers.** Some nonzero residue vector leaves at most the average number
of rows: `rows left · ∏ (r - 1) ≤ |P| · ∏ (r - 2)`. -/
theorem exists_rowsLeft_le (S P : Finset ℕ) (hS : ∀ r ∈ S, 2 ≤ r)
    (hP : ∀ q ∈ P, ∀ r ∈ S, ¬ r ∣ q) :
    ∃ b ∈ vectors S, #(rowsLeft S P b) * ∏ r ∈ S, (r - 1) ≤ #P * ∏ r ∈ S, (r - 2) :=
  Finset.exists_le_of_sum_le (vectors_nonempty S hS)
    (f := fun b => #(rowsLeft S P b) * ∏ r ∈ S, (r - 1))
    (g := fun _ => #P * ∏ r ∈ S, (r - 2))
    (le_of_eq (sum_card_rowsLeft_mul S P (fun r hr => by
      have := hS r hr
      omega) hP))

note.text: Sets the baseline: a random-like cover leaves this many rows. Anything better has to be searched for.

nodes.title: No free lunch for the choice of moduli
nodes.gist: For moduli of at least 3, the average over residue vectors of (rows left × ∏ r/(r − 1)) is at least |P|/2. No choice of moduli improves the average.
nodes.detail: So an averaging argument cannot be sharpened by picking better moduli. To beat the average you need a special design, and finding one is the hard search problem.
nodes.source:
/-- **No free lunch.** For moduli `≥ 3` and rows not divisible by any of them, the average
over nonzero residue vectors of `rows left × ∏ r/(r - 1)` is at least `|P| / 2`:
`|P| · (number of vectors) · ∏ (r - 1) ≤ 2 · (Σ_b rows left) · ∏ r`. No choice of moduli
improves the average. -/
theorem noFreeLunch (S P : Finset ℕ) (hS : ∀ r ∈ S, 3 ≤ r)
    (hP : ∀ q ∈ P, ∀ r ∈ S, ¬ r ∣ q) :
    #P * (#(vectors S) * ∏ r ∈ S, (r - 1)) ≤
      2 * ((∑ b ∈ vectors S, #(rowsLeft S P b)) * ∏ r ∈ S, r) := by
  rw [sum_card_rowsLeft S P (fun r hr => by
    have := hS r hr
    omega) hP, card_vectors]
  have h := prod_pred_sq_le S hS
  rw [Finset.prod_pow, Finset.prod_mul_distrib] at h
  generalize (∏ r ∈ S, (r - 1)) = V at h ⊢
  generalize (∏ r ∈ S, (r - 2)) = W at h ⊢
  generalize (∏ r ∈ S, r) = R at h ⊢
  calc #P * (V * V) = #P * V ^ 2 := by ring
    _ ≤ #P * (2 * (R * W)) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ h
    _ = 2 * (#P * W * R) := by ring

note.text: Says that different moduli cannot improve the average. Any improvement has to come from structure in the design.

nodes.title: Layered covers (Erdős–Rankin style)
nodes.gist: Split the moduli into a fixed layer F, a pigeonhole layer S and a mop-up layer T. If a counting inequality holds, the classes on F extend to a full cover of every row.
nodes.detail: The formal heart of the asymptotic covering bounds: the first layer kills most rows, the second handles the survivors by averaging, the third finishes them. Proved from the first-moment pigeonhole. Since 24 Nov the classes are stated on their own (exists_classes_of_layers), before the numbers N are built from them, so the covering bound can be read as a statement about the cover depth.
nodes.source:
/-- **Layered covers.** Let `F`, `S`, `T` be pairwise disjoint sets of moduli, the moduli of

nodes.title: From a cover to a number below a cap
nodes.gist: If classes modulo odd primes r ≤ B cover the odd primes below Q, then some even N in all the classes with Q + B < N ≤ Q + B + 2·∏r has no Goldbach summand below Q.

nodes.title: What survives a fixed layer is smooth or nearly
nodes.gist: If every prime factor of n < w² is ≤ z or > w, then n is z-smooth, or n = A·p′ with p′ > w prime and A z-smooth. In row form: q − 1 is smooth, or q = A·p′ + 1.
nodes.detail: Step E4 of the Erdős–Rankin adaptation. It lets the rows left by the fixed layer be counted by smooth numbers and prime pairs.
nodes.source:
/-- **Structure of the rows surviving a fixed layer** (step (E4) of the Erdős–Rankin
adaptation). If every prime factor of `n` is `≤ z` or `> w`, and `n < w²`, then either `n` is
`z`-smooth, or `n = A · p'` with `p' > w` prime and `A` `z`-smooth. -/
theorem smooth_or_large_prime_factor {n z w : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hlt : n < w * w)
    (h : ∀ p, p.Prime → p ∣ n → p ≤ z ∨ w < p) :
    (∀ p, p.Prime → p ∣ n → p ≤ z) ∨
      ∃ p' A, p'.Prime ∧ w < p' ∧ n = A * p' ∧ ∀ p, p.Prime → p ∣ A → p ≤ z := by
  by_cases hall : ∀ p, p.Prime → p ∣ n → p ≤ z
  · exact Or.inl hall
  · right
    have hex : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n ∧ z < p := by
      by_contra hcon
      exact hall fun p hp hd => by
        by_contra hlt'
        exact hcon ⟨p, hp, hd, by omega⟩

nodes.title: Polynomial families are too sparse
nodes.gist: If f(c) ≥ c² for all c in a set T, and all the values f(c) are below Q, then T has at most √Q + 1 elements.
nodes.detail: With Q the row bound, this limits how many rows a family of degree 2 or more can remove. With Q the cap, it limits how many members the family has. Also proved: if N = f(u) and q = f(c) then N − q is divisible by u − c, hence composite when 1 < u − c < N − q.
nodes.source:
/-- **The value-set ceiling.** If `f(c) ≥ c²` for every `c` in a finite set `T` and all the
values `f(c)`, `c ∈ T`, are below `Q`, then `T` has at most `√Q + 1` elements. With `Q` the
row bound this limits the rows a family of degree `≥ 2` can remove; with `Q = X` the cap, it
limits the number of members of the family. -/
theorem card_le_sqrt_succ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (Q : ℕ) (T : Finset ℕ)
    (hT : ∀ c ∈ T, c ^ 2 ≤ f c ∧ f c < Q) : T.card ≤ Nat.sqrt Q + 1 := by
  rw [← Finset.card_range (Nat.sqrt Q + 1)]
  refine Finset.card_le_card fun c hc => ?_
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hT c hc
  rw [Finset.mem_range, Nat.lt_succ_iff, Nat.le_sqrt']
  omega

nodes.title: A prime gap gives a Goldbach gap
nodes.gist: If no prime lies strictly between p and p′ then p′ + 1 has no Goldbach summand up to p′ − p; and if p and p′ − p + 1 are prime, then g(p′ + 1) = p′ − p + 1.
nodes.detail: Ties g(N) to prime gaps: a very large prime gap automatically produces a number with large least summand. A different route from covering.
nodes.source:
theorem not_isSummand_of_desert {p p' q : ℕ} (hgap : ∀ n, p < n → n < p' → ¬ n.Prime)
    (hq : q ≤ p' - p) : ¬ IsSummand (p' + 1) q := by
  rintro ⟨hqp, hN⟩
  have h2 := hqp.two_le
  exact hgap (p' + 1 - q) (by omega) (by omega) hN

nodes.title: Expected successes = Σ (1 − p)^(rows left)
nodes.gist: If each leftover row is prime with probability p, then for any chosen set of candidates the expected number of successes is the sum over candidates of (1 − p)^(rows left).
nodes.detail: The 'logged hit mass' printed by the search runs is exactly the expected number of successes. This is the cost model of the capped game.
nodes.source:
/-- **The logged hit mass is the expected number of successes.** For every set `T` of
selected members, member `k` having the rows `A k` left:
`E [number of k ∈ T all of whose rows are composite] = Σ_{k ∈ T} (1 - p)^{|A k|}`. -/
theorem expected_hits (p : ℝ) (T : Finset κ) (A : κ → Finset ι) :
    ∑ ω : ι → Bool, bern p ω * (∑ k ∈ T, ∏ i ∈ A k, if ω i then (0 : ℝ) else 1) =
      ∑ k ∈ T, (1 - p) ^ #(A k) := by
  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => sum_bern_all_false p (A k)

nodes.title: Selection identity: where the successes sit
nodes.gist: If rows-left is Gaussian over candidates, those at least z standard deviations below the mean hold the fraction Φ(λ − z) of all the success probability, where λ = −√v·ln(1 − p).

nodes.title: Tilt: what the best candidate is worth
nodes.gist: A candidate z standard deviations below the mean in rows left is e^(λz − λ²/2) times likelier to succeed than average. Among K candidates the best has z ≈ √(2 ln K), so picking the best gains only about λ·√(2 ln K) nats.
nodes.detail: A nat is a factor of e in the odds. The gain from picking the best of K candidates grows like √(ln K), not like K. Choosing promising candidates helps a little and cannot replace more search.
nodes.source:
/-- **What the best member is worth.** A member whose number of rows left is `z` standard
deviations below the mean is `e^(λ z - λ²/2)` times as likely to succeed as an average member,
`λ = -√v ln (1 - p)`. Among `K` members the best has `z ≈ √(2 ln K)`, so no search inside a
progression of `K` members gains more than about `λ √(2 ln K)` nats over testing at random. -/
theorem enrichment_at (μ : ℝ) {v : ℝ≥0} (hv : v ≠ 0) {p : ℝ} (hp : p < 1) (z : ℝ) :
    (1 - p) ^ (μ - z * √(v : ℝ)) / (∫ r, (1 - p) ^ r ∂(gaussianReal μ v)) =
      rexp (-(√(v : ℝ) * Real.log (1 - p)) * z - (√(v : ℝ) * Real.log (1 - p)) ^ 2 / 2) := by
  have hpos : 0 < 1 - p := by linarith
  have hpow : ∀ r : ℝ, (1 - p) ^ r = rexp (Real.log (1 - p) * r) :=
    fun r => Real.rpow_def_of_pos hpos r
  simp_rw [hpow]
  rw [integral_exp_mul_gaussianReal μ hv, ← Real.exp_sub]
  congr 1
  have := Real.mul_self_sqrt v.coe_nonneg
  linear_combination (Real.log (1 - p) ^ 2 / 2) * this

nodes.title: Lattice decoding radius
nodes.gist: For k rows and sieve primes up to z ≥ k/e, a lattice method needs the smooth part of the leftover to be c times the typical one with c² ≥ e·ln K/4. For K = 2^32 candidates that means c ≥ 3.88.
nodes.detail: Quantifies how good a lattice-based construction of N would have to be: numbers almost four times smoother than typical.
nodes.source:
/-- **The decoding radius of the lattice method.** `k` rows, sieve primes up to `z ≥ k/e`,
typical smooth exponent `β_typ = (k/z)(1 + ln (z/k))`. If the condition `ln K ≤ z β² / k` of
the method holds for `β = c β_typ`, then `c² ≥ e ln K / 4`. -/
theorem lattice_radius {k z c lnK : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) (hz : k * exp (-1) ≤ z)
    (h : lnK ≤ z * (c * (k / z * (1 + log (z / k)))) ^ 2 / k) :
    exp 1 * lnK / 4 ≤ c ^ 2 := by
  have hz0 : 0 < z := lt_of_lt_of_le (mul_pos hk (exp_pos _)) hz
  have hx : exp (-1) ≤ z / k := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ hk]
    linarith
  have hx0 : 0 < z / k := div_pos hz0 hk
  have h1 := one_add_log_sq_le hx
  have e : z * (c * (k / z * (1 + log (z / k)))) ^ 2 / k =
      c ^ 2 * ((1 + log (z / k)) ^ 2 / (z / k)) := by
    field_simp
  rw [e] at h
  have h2 : (1 + log (z / k)) ^ 2 / (z / k) ≤ 4 / exp 1 := by
    rw [div_le_iff₀ hx0]
    exact h1
  have h3 : lnK ≤ c ^ 2 * (4 / exp 1) :=
    h.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2 (sq_nonneg c))
  have he : 0 < exp 1 := ex

nodes.title: Partial information costs more than it earns
nodes.gist: Restricting N to a list of ℓ classes modulo r (2 ≤ ℓ ≤ r/2) costs ln(r/ℓ) nats of search space but contributes only ln r/ℓ to the lattice condition. The cost exceeds the credit by at least ln 2 − 2 ln r/r.
nodes.detail: The inequality behind the next theorem.
nodes.source:
/-- **An informative list is outside the radius.** A list of `ℓ` classes modulo `r` with
`2 ≤ ℓ ≤ r/2` carries `ln (r/ℓ)` nats of information and contributes `ln r / ℓ` to the lattice
condition; the first exceeds the second by at least `ln 2 - 2 ln r / r`. -/
theorem list_deficit {r l : ℝ} (hr : 16 ≤ r) (h2 : 2 ≤ l) (hl : l ≤ r / 2) :
    log r / l + (log 2 - 2 * log r / r) ≤ log (r / l) := by
  have hr0 : 0 < r := by linarith
  have hl0 : 0 < l := by linarith
  have hlogr : 4 * log 2 ≤ log r := by
    have h16 : log 16 = 4 * log 2 := by
      rw [show (16 : ℝ) = 2 ^ (4 : ℕ) by norm_num, Real.log_pow]
      norm_num
    rw [← h16]
    exact Real.log_le_log (by norm_num) hr
  have hlog2 : 0 < log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)

  have hu2 : 2 ≤ u := by
    rw [hu, le_div_iff₀ hl0]
    linarith
  have hur : u ≤ r / 2 := by
    rw [hu, div_le_div_iff₀ hl0 (by norm_num)]
    nlinarith
  have hrl : log r / l = log r / r

nodes.title: Black-box bound: no free search
nodes.gist: Among K candidates with g good ones, any strategy that asks m questions finds a good one on at most the fraction m·g/K of the possible arrangements.
nodes.detail: Without structure to exploit, finding a good candidate takes about K/g questions. The formal version of 'there is no shortcut by queries alone'.
nodes.source:
/-- **The black-box bound.** Of the `C(K, g)` possible sets of `g` good members, `m` questions
find a good member for at most the fraction `m g / K`. -/
theorem blackbox_fraction (K g m : ℕ) (hK : 1 ≤ K) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (t : Fin m → Fin K) :
    (((univ : Finset (Fin K)).powersetCard g).filter (fun G => ∃ j, t j ∈ G)).card * K ≤
      m * g * K.choose g := by
  obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ : ∃ n, K = n + 1 := ⟨K - 1, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k, g = k + 1 := ⟨g - 1, by omega⟩
  have h := blackbox_bound (n + 1) (k + 1) m t
  simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel] at h
  have e := Nat.add_one_mul_choose_eq n k
  calc _ ≤ m * n.choose k * (n + 1) := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h
    _ = m * ((n + 1) * n.choose k) := by ring
    _ = m * ((n + 1).choose (k + 1) * (k + 1)) := by rw [e]
    _ = m * (k + 1) * (n + 1).choose (k + 1) := by ring

nodes.title: No selection beats the population
nodes.gist: Whichever candidates are tested, their hit mass is at most |S|·y^k plus the hit mass of all candidates with fewer than k rows left.
nodes.detail: The only way to gain is to find candidates with unusually few leftover rows. Testing a cleverly chosen subset gets no more than the tail of the population allows.

nodes.title: Few rows left is rare
nodes.gist: With μ the mean number of rows left, a candidate has at most μ − a rows left with probability at most exp(−a²/(2μ)).
nodes.detail: A concentration bound: candidates with unusually few leftover rows are exponentially rare.

/-- **Few rows left is rare.** With `μ = ∑ s_j > 0` the mean number of rows left: a member has
at most `k ≤ μ - a` rows left with probability at most `exp (-a² / (2 μ))`. -/
theorem prob_patternRows_le {s : ι → ℝ} (hs0 : ∀ j, 0 ≤ s j) (hs1 : ∀ j, s j ≤ 1) {a : ℝ}

nodes.title: Meet-in-the-middle price
nodes.gist: Merging two lists of a and b partial designs costs at least a + b ≥ 2√(ab), and yields K·a·b/P complete candidates on average, so the cost per candidate is at least 2P/(K·√(ab)).
nodes.detail: The best possible price for combining partial designs by merging. Any sublinear trick has to beat this.
nodes.source:
/-- Merging two lists of `a` and `b` entries costs at least `a + b`, and `a + b ≥ 2 √(a b)`;
the merge yields `K a b / P` members on average. So the cost per member found is at least
`2 P / (K √(a b))`. -/
theorem mitm_cost {a b P K : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hP : 0 < P) (hK : 0 < K) :
    2 * P / (K * Real.sqrt (a * b)) ≤ (a + b) / (K * (a * b) / P) := by
  have hab : 0 < a * b := mul_pos ha hb
  have hs : 0 < Real.sqrt (a * b) := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hab
  have hss : Real.sqrt (a * b) * Real.sqrt (a * b) = a * b := Real.mul_self_sqrt hab.le
  have hamgm : 2 * Real.sqrt (a * b) ≤ a + b := by
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - b), sq_nonneg (a + b - 2 * Real.sqrt (a * b)), mul_pos ha hb]
  rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (mul_pos hK hs) (div_pos (mul_pos hK hab) hP)]
  have e1 : 2 * P * (K * (a * b) / P) = 2 * K * (a * b) := by
    field_simp
  rw [e1]
  have e2 : 2 * K * (a * b) = K * Real.sqrt (a * b) * (2 * Real.sqrt (a * b)) := by
    linear_combination (-2 * K) * hss
  rw [e2, mul_comm (a + b)]

nodes.title: One prime buys few rows

nodes.detail: W is the most rows any one class kills and μ the average over all classes. A nat is a factor of e.

nodes.title: Above Q no list pays
nodes.gist: For a prime s ≥ 213,070 every class kills at most one row. With at most 1,609 rows left (the best covers at the 10% target), restricting N to a list of classes gains at most 0.207 rows per nat spent.
nodes.detail: Closes one tempting way to spend leftover budget: putting constraints on primes above the cover.
nodes.source:
/-- **Above `Q` no list pays.** For a prime `s ≥ 213070` every class kills at most one row. If
at most `1609` rows are left (the best covers at the 10% target), then for every list `L` of

nodes.title: Brainstorm: what a kernel could decide among 100 ideas
nodes.gist: On 2026-11-22 the research session sent 100 ideas for raising the record and asked the Lean session to try to prove each one wrong. Twenty-one of them contained a theorem; this file holds those, numbered as in the list.
nodes.detail: Examples. One exponent serves every row: N − q passes the base-2 Fermat test exactly when 2^(N−1) ≡ 2^q modulo it, so a scanner can reuse one exponent for all rows of N (fermat_common_exponent). No stopping rule helps: abandoning a candidate never spends fewer tests per success than never abandoning (never_abandon). Moves under the cap keep at most three new rows (move_keeps_at_most_three). For primes of 213,070 or more, a divisor shared by two rows is impossible (large_divisors_unique). The rest of the list is engineering, measurement or heuristic counting with no theorem in it.

/-- **Idea 28.** The row `N - q` (odd) passes the base-2 Fermat test iff
`2^(N-1) ≡ 2^q` modulo it: the exponent `N - 1` serves every row of `N`. -/
theorem fermat_common_exponent {N q : ℕ} (hq : q < N) (hodd : (N - q) % 2 = 1) :
    2 ^ (N - 1) ≡ 2 ^ q [MOD N - q] ↔ 2 ^ (N - q - 1) ≡ 1 [MOD N - q] := by
  have he : N - 1 = (N - q - 1) + q := by omega
  have h2 : Nat.Coprime (N - q) 2 := by
    rw [Nat.coprime_comm, Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd Nat.prime_two]
    omega
  have hc : Nat.Coprime (N - q) (2 ^ q) := Nat.Coprime.pow_right q h2
  rw [he, pow_add]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h' : 2 ^ (N - q - 1) * 2 ^ q ≡ 1 * 2 ^ q [MOD N - q] := by simpa using h
    exact Nat.ModEq.cancel_right_of_coprime hc h'
  · intro h
    simpa using h.mul_right (2 ^ q)

nodes.title: A failed Fermat test proves a number composite
nodes.gist: If 2^(m−1) mod m is not 1, then m is not prime. This lets a record show that thousands of 200-digit rows are composite by checking one modular power each.
nodes.detail: Only this direction is needed: a failed test is a proof, a passed test proves nothing. The record files list, for the rows left by the cover, which ones are shown composite this way, and the kernel recomputes each one.
nodes.source:
/-- A number that fails the base-2 Fermat test is not an odd prime. -/
theorem not_prime_of_powMod_ne_one {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 < m) (h : powMod 2 (m - 1) m ≠ 1) :
    ¬ m.Prime := by
  intro hp
  apply h
  have hcop : Nat.Coprime 2 m := (Nat.coprime_primes Nat.prime_two hp).mpr (by omega)
  have := Nat.ModEq.pow_totient hcop
  rw [Nat.totient_prime hp] at this
  rw [powMod_def]
  exact Eq.trans this (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega))

nodes.title: Block check: no summand in a range of q
nodes.gist: A computable check for a block of consecutive values q: each N − q is divisible by a covering modulus, or by a small prime, or fails the Fermat test. If the check returns true, no q in the block is a Goldbach summand.

theorem noSummandIn_of_desertBlockCheck {N g lo len : ℕ}

    (hlists : desertListsCheck N g coverMods smallPrimes = true)
    (h : desertBlockCheck N lo len coverMods smallPrimes residuals = true)

  simp only [desertListsCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, List.all_eq_true] at hlists
  obtain ⟨⟨hN, hsmall⟩, hcover⟩ := hlists
  simp only [desertBlockCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true, beq_iff_eq, bne_iff_ne] at h

nodes.title: Complete certificate for g(N) = g
nodes.gist: If no prime below g is a summand of N, and g and N − g are both prime, then g is the least Goldbach summand of N.
nodes.detail: Glues the two halves of a record: the negative side (block checks for everything below g) and the positive side (primality of g and of N − g).
nodes.source:
/-- A complete certificate for `g(N) = g`: the negative side by block checks, the positive
side by the primality of `g` and of the complement `N - g`. -/
theorem isLeastSummand_of_noSummandIn {N g : ℕ} (h : NoSummandIn N 0 g) (hg : g.Prime)
    (hc : (N - g).Prime) : IsLeastSummand N g :=
  ⟨⟨hg, hc⟩, fun p hp => not_lt.mp fun hlt => h p (Nat.zero_le p) hlt hp⟩

nodes.title: A covered range has no summand
nodes.gist: If every q in a range has N − q divisible by a proper divisor (a covering modulus), then no q in the range is a Goldbach summand. A block test with an empty residual list certifies exactly this.
nodes.detail: Used for the pure cover (15,907) where no Fermat tests are needed at all. It is the divisibility-only half of the block check.
nodes.source:
/-- A covered range has no Goldbach summand: each `N - q` has the proper divisor `r`. -/
theorem CoveredIn.noSummandIn {N g a b : ℕ} {coverMods smallPrimes : List ℕ}
    (hlists : desertListsCheck N g coverMods smallPrimes = true)
    (h : CoveredIn N coverMods a b) (hb : b ≤ g) : NoSummandIn N a b := by
  simp only [desertListsCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, List.all_eq_true] at hlists
  obtain ⟨-, hcover⟩ := hlists
  rintro q ha hb' ⟨hqp, hNq⟩
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrq⟩ := h q ha hb' hqp
  have hr2 := hcover r hr
  rcases (Nat.dvd_prime hNq).mp hrq with h1 | h1 <;> omega

nodes.title: Elliptic-curve primality: one step is sound
nodes.gist: If q is prime and a point on an elliptic curve modulo N behaves as the certificate says, then N is prime. A chain of 26 steps proves that the 200-digit N − 158,209 is prime.
nodes.detail: A kernel-checkable Atkin–Morain/Goldwasser–Kilian criterion in the format PARI/GP prints. theorem prime_of_stepCheck {N a x y s q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (h : stepCheck N a x y s q = true) :

  simp only [stepCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h

    ⟨_, rfl⟩

nodes.title: Pure cover: no prime below 15,907 is a summand
nodes.gist: A 193-digit even N such that for every prime q below 15,907 the number N − q has a divisor between 2 and 463. No primality or compositeness test is needed, only divisibility.
nodes.detail: This is what a cover alone certifies, with no luck involved. It uses the 89 odd primes up to 463. The same N also appears as a number below 10^200. The record 160,357 reaches about ten times further by using a cover that leaves some rows alive, then searching millions of candidates for one where every leftover row happens to be composite.
nodes.source:
/-- **The complete cover.** `N` is even, has 193 digits, and for every prime `q < 15907` the
number `N - q` has a divisor `r` with `2 ≤ r ≤ 463` (so it is composite: `r < N - q`). -/
theorem complete_cover :
    N < 10 ^ 193 ∧ Even N ∧
      (∀ q < 15907, q.Prime → ∃ r, 2 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ 463 ∧ r < N - q ∧ r ∣ N - q) ∧
      ∀ q < 15907, ¬ IsSummand N q := by
  have hl := lists
  simp only [desertListsCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, List.all_eq_true] at hl
  refine ⟨N_lt, N_even, fun q hq hqp => ?_, fun q hq => noSummand q (Nat.zero_le q) hq⟩
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrq⟩ := covered q (Nat.zero_le q) hq hqp
  have h2 := hl.2 r hr
  have hQ : Q = 15907 := rfl
  exact ⟨r, h2.1, coverMods_le r hr, by omega, hrq⟩

nodes.title: Stickelberger–Swan theorem over any finite field
nodes.gist: For a squarefree polynomial over a finite field of odd characteristic, whether its number of irreducible factors is even or odd is decided by whether its discriminant is a square.

nodes.title: Discriminant of N − Q when N has zero derivative
nodes.gist: If N′ = 0 and Q is monic of smaller degree, with every irreducible factor of Q′ dividing N, then disc(N − Q) = ± λ^(n−d−1)·d^(n−d)·disc(Q).
nodes.detail: In characteristic p a polynomial N = c·V^p has zero derivative, so the discriminant of N − Q depends only on Q. The algebraic fact behind the function-field desert.
nodes.source:
/-- **The discriminant identity.** Over any field: if `N' = 0`, `Q` is monic of degree `d`
with `d ≠ 0` in the field and `d < n = deg N`, and every irreducible factor of `Q'` divides
`N`, then `discr (N - Q) = ± λ^(n-d-1) d^(n-d) discr Q` with the sign below. -/
theorem discr_sub {N Q : F[X]} (hQ : Q.Monic) (hN : derivative N = 0)
    (hd : (Q.natDegree : F) ≠ 0) (hlt : Q.natDegree < N.natDegree)
    (hrad : ∀ π : F[X], Irreducible π → π ∣ derivative Q → π ∣ N) :
    discr (N - Q) =
      (-1) ^ (N.natDegree * (N.natDegree - 1) / 2 + N.natDegree * Q.natDegree
          + (Q.natDegree - 1) + Q.natDegree * (Q.natDegree - 1) / 2)
        * N.leadingCoeff ^ (N.natDegree - Q.natDegree - 1)
        * (Q.natDegree : F) ^ (N.natDegree - Q.natDegree) * discr Q :=
  discr_sub_aux rfl rfl rfl hQ hN hd hlt hrad

nodes.title: Parity theorem for N − Q
nodes.gist: Under those hypotheses with Q irreducible, N − Q is squarefree, and the parity of its number of irreducible factors is fixed by the degrees and by quadratic characters of −1, of N's leading coefficient and of deg Q.
nodes.detail: Combines the discriminant identity with Stickelberger–Swan.
nodes.source:
theorem parity_card_factors (hF : ringChar F ≠ 2) {N Q : F[X]}
    (hQ : Q.Monic) (hQi : Irreducible Q) (hN : derivative N = 0)
    (hd : (Q.natDegree : F) ≠ 0) (hlt : Q.natDegree < N.natDegree)
    (hrad : ∀ π : F[X], Irreducible π → π ∣ derivative Q → π ∣ N) :
    Squarefree (N - Q) ∧
      (-1 : ℤ) ^ (N.natDegree + Multiset.card (normalizedFactors (N - Q))) =
        quadraticChar F (-1) ^ (N.natDegree * (N.natDegree - 1) / 2 + N.natDegree * Q.natDegree
            + (Q.natDegree - 1) + Q.natDegree * (Q.natDegree - 1) / 2)
          * quadraticChar F N.leadingCoeff ^ (N.natDegree - Q.natDegree - 1)
          * quadraticChar F (Q.natDegree : F) ^ (N.natDegree - Q.natDegree)
          * (-1) ^ (Q.natDegree + 1) := by
  have hsq := squarefree_sub hQi hN (derivative_ne_zero_of_monic hQ hd) hrad
  refine ⟨hsq, ?_⟩

  have h2 := stickelbergerSwan F hF Q hQi.squarefree
  rw [normalizedFactors_irreducible hQi, Multiset.card_singleton] at h2

nodes.title: Corollary: N − Q is reducible
nodes.gist: Over a finite field of odd characteristic with a square number of elements, if N's leading coefficient is not a square, then N − Q is not irreducible.
nodes.detail: Parity makes the factor count even, so it cannot be one.
nodes.source:
/-- **Corollary.** Over a finite field of odd characteristic with a square number of elements:
if the leading coefficient of `N` is not a square, `N - Q` is not irreducible. -/
theorem not_irreducible_sub_of_isSquare_card (hF : ringChar F ≠ 2)
    (hq : IsSquare (Fintype.card F)) {N Q : F[X]}
    (hQ : Q.Monic) (hQi : Irreducible Q) (hN : derivative N = 0)
    (hd : (Q.natDegree : F) ≠ 0) (hlt : Q.natDegree < N.natDegree)
    (hrad : ∀ π : F[X], Irreducible π → π ∣ derivative Q → π ∣ N)
    (hlam : ¬IsSquare N.leadingCoeff) :
    ¬Irreducible (N - Q) :=
  not_irreducible_sub hF hQ hQi hN hd hlt hrad
    (by simpa using isSquare_intCast_of_isSquare_card hF hq (-1))
    (by simpa using isSquare_intCast_of_isSquare_card hF hq (Q.natDegree : ℤ)) hlam

nodes.title: The function-field desert
nodes.gist: Take N = c·V^p with c a non-square and V divisible by every irreducible polynomial of degree at most J. Then N − Q is reducible for every irreducible Q of degree at most J + 1: one degree more than divisibility alone gives.
nodes.detail: The setting is a finite field of odd characteristic p with a square number of elements. Degrees up to J are covered by divisibility, as in the integer cover. The extra degree J + 1 is covered by parity alone, with no divisor exhibited (allowed when p does not divide it). This is the function-field counterpart of the primorial core, with a parity bonus.
nodes.source:
/-- **The desert.** Over a finite field of odd characteristic `p` with a square number of
elements, let `V` be monic and divisible by every irreducible polynomial of degree at most `J`
(for instance their product), `c` a non-square, and `N = c · V^p`. Then `N - Q` is not
irreducible for every monic irreducible `Q` of degree at most `J + 1` and less than `deg N`,
the degree `J + 1` being allowed when `p` does not divide it. For `deg Q ≤ J` the factor is
`Q` itself; for `deg Q = J + 1` no factor is exhibited. -/
theorem desert (hF : ringChar F ≠ 2)

nodes.title: Discriminant of N − Q as a resultant
nodes.gist: For any N with N′ = 0 and Q′ ≠ 0, disc(N − Q) = ± λ^(n−2−e)·Res(Q′, N − Q), where e = deg Q′. The discriminant, of degree 2n − 2 in the coefficients, is a resultant with a polynomial of lower degree.
nodes.detail: The latest Lean addition on the Lean branch (2026-11-23, 14:55 UTC). It removes the hypothesis that the roots of Q′ divide N, so the parity of N − Q is controlled for every N with zero derivative.
nodes.source:
/-- **The discriminant of `N - Q` for `N' = 0`, in general.** Over any field, with no condition
on the roots of `Q'`: if `N' = 0`, `Q' ≠ 0` and `deg Q < n = deg N`, then with `λ` the leading
coefficient of `N` and `e = deg Q'`,
`discr (N - Q) = (-1)^(n(n-1)/2 + n + ne) · λ^(n-2-e) · Res(Q', N - Q)`.
So the discriminant, a quantity of degree `2n - 2` in the coefficients, is a resultant with the
derivative of the row, a polynomial of degree below `deg Q`. -/
theorem discr_sub_eq_resultant {N Q : F[X]} (hN : derivative N = 0) (hQ' : derivative Q ≠ 0)
    (hlt : Q.natDegree < N.natDegree) :
    discr (N - Q) =
      (-1) ^ (N.natDegree * (N.natDegree - 1) / 2 + N.natDegree
          + N.natDegree * (derivative Q).natDegree)
        * N.leadingCoeff ^ (N.natDegree - 2 - (derivative Q).natDegree)
        * resultant (derivative Q) (N - Q) (derivative Q).natDegree N.natDegree :=
  discr_sub_eq_resultant_aux rfl rfl rfl hN hQ' hlt

nodes.title: The exponent schedule never forms n − 1
nodes.gist: The kernels test 2^(n−1) ≡ 1 without ever building the exponent n − 1: they start from a power of two and double at the right steps. This proves the final value is 1 exactly when the Fermat test passes.
nodes.detail: Proved for a general Montgomery radix R = 2^Rb, so one lemma serves the 104-bit, 90-bit and 672-bit kernels.
nodes.source:
/-- The test the code makes: `y t ≡ 1` exactly when `2^(n-1) ≡ 1 (mod n)`. -/
theorem schedule_iff {n t : ℕ} (hodd : n % 2 = 1) (hc : cOf n t ≤ 104) (y : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h0 : y 0 ≡ 2 ^ (104 - cOf n t) [MOD n])
    (hstep : ∀ i < t, 2 ^ 104 * y (i + 1) ≡ 2 ^ beta n t (i + 1) * y i ^ 2 [MOD n]) :
    y t ≡ 1 [MOD n] ↔ 2 ^ (n - 1) ≡ 1 [MOD n] :=
  schedule_iffR (by norm_num) hodd hc y h0 hstep

nodes.title: Thinning above Q: independence is a safe bound
nodes.gist: For moduli that separate the rows (every modulus at least Q, with rows below Q), the number of class vectors that kill every row is at most ∏m·(1 − θ)^k, exactly what independent killing would give. So independence can only overstate how often few rows are left.
nodes.detail: The reason is Bernoulli's inequality: a modulus that separates the rows kills at most one of them. Inside the residue model this turns the cost model's independence assumption into an inequality for the primes above Q; the gap is about (k·p)²·Σ1/m²/2, below 10^-5 for k up to 2,000, p = 0.07 and moduli above 10^8 (an estimate, not proved). Below Q two rows can share a class and the inequality is not a theorem. A binomial Chernoff form is included. The Lean session's thinning_check script reports that each deeper level of the research prize table follows from a shallower one within 0.14–1.35 nats.

/-- **Above `Q` independent thinning is an upper bound.** For rows below `Q` and moduli
`≥ Q ≥ 1`: the sum over class vectors of `y ^ (rows left)` is at most
`∏ m · (1 - (1 - y) θ)^|S|` for `0 ≤ y ≤ 1`. -/
theorem thinSum_le_of_lt {y : ℝ} (hy0 : 0 ≤ y) (hy1 : y ≤ 1) {Q : ℕ} (hQ : 0 < Q)
    (ms : List ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ) (hms : ∀ m ∈ ms, Q ≤ m) (hS : ∀ q ∈ S, q < Q) :
    thinSum y ms S ≤ (ms.prod : ℕ) * (1 - (1 - y) * survival ms) ^ #S :=
  thinSum_le hy0 hy1 ms S (fun m h => lt_of_lt_of_le hQ (hms m h))
    fun m h => injOn_mod_of_lt hS (hms m h)

nodes.title: Needles closer than Q are not independent
nodes.gist: A needle at level Q is an N with no Goldbach summand below Q. If N is a needle, N + h inherits every row N + h − q′ with q′ − h prime and below Q, so it only needs its other rows to be composite. Needles at distance Q or more share no row.
nodes.detail: At Q = 1,000, N + 30 inherits 97 of its 168 rows. In the exhaustive miniature (N below 10^9, 303 needles), independent uniform positions give 0.09 pairs closer than 1,000, counting inherited rows as certain gives 2.7, and there are four, at distances 30, 30, 126 and 210, certified in the kernel. Nothing here says needles are random: that nothing else distinguishes them is a form of the prime tuples conjecture, which is open.
nodes.source:
/-- **A neighbour of a needle is a needle as soon as its rows that are not inherited are
composite.** The rows `q'` with `q' - h` prime need no test. -/
theorem IsNeedle.add_of_forall {N Q h : ℕ} (hN : IsNeedle N Q)
    (hrest : ∀ q' < Q, q'.Prime → ¬ (h ≤ q' ∧ (q' - h).Prime) → ¬ (N + h - q').Prime) :
    IsNeedle (N + h) Q := by
  intro q' hq' hs
  by_cases hin : h ≤ q' ∧ (q' - h).Prime
  · exact hN.not_isSummand_add hin.1 hin.2 (by omega) hs
  · exact hrest q' hq' hs.1 hin hs.2

nodes.title: Record holders up to 10^12, and the shift law
nodes.gist: The 42 even numbers up to 10^12 whose least Goldbach summand beats every smaller even number, each certified in the kernel (N − q composite for every prime q < g by an exhibited divisor; g and N − g prime). They agree with terms 2 to 43 of OEIS A025018 and A025019.
nodes.detail: An experiment the Lean session ran at the user's request. Alongside the table, exact relations visible in the arrivals: if 3 does not divide N then 3 divides N + g(N); g(N) is at least the distance to the previous prime; and the shift law g(N + h) ≤ g(N) + h, with equality when the rows not inherited from N are composite (four certified pairs, such as 480,878 and 480,908). A statistical pattern, that arrivals prefer residue classes that are quadratic non-residues, is explained by a finite check of Chebyshev's bias up to level 4,096. That no smaller number does better is a theorem below 2^25 (see the sieve box); beyond it, up to 10^12, it is a scan, not a theorem.

nodes.title: A record is a cover: the exact test for "N beats G"
nodes.gist: An even N has no Goldbach summand up to G exactly when its residues modulo the primes up to its square root cover the strikers: for every prime q ≤ G some prime r has N ≡ q (mod r). A walker over N = 4, 6, 8, … that asks only this question announces exactly the terms of A025018.
nodes.detail: The walker keeps one number G, the largest least summand met so far, and announces N when its least summand exceeds G (mem_walk, for every bound X; walk_sorted). The same question has two equivalent forms: no prime within G below N lies at a prime distance from N, and the covering form above (beats_iff_wheels). The covering form is the condition the 200-digit certificates establish. Below 2^20 the walker announces 21 numbers (4, 6, 12, 30, 98, …, 503,222), checked through the kernel run of the sieve. A C version (scripts/record_gen/ngen.c) walks to 5·10^12 in 83 minutes on three cores and announces 46 terms, equal to the OEIS b-file; it cannot skip, because passing a number means finding a Goldbach partition for it.
nodes.source:
/-- **The question, asked of `N` alone.** `N` has no Goldbach summand up to `G` exactly when
its residues modulo the small primes cover the strikers: for every prime `q ≤ G` there is a
prime `r` with `r² ≤ N - q` and `N ≡ q (mod r)`. -/
theorem beats_iff_wheels {N G : ℕ} (hG : G + 2 ≤ N) :
    (∀ q ≤ G, ¬ IsSummand N q) ↔
      ∀ q ≤ G, q.Prime → ∃ r, r.Prime ∧ r * r ≤ N - q ∧ N % r = q % r := by
  constructor
  · intro h q hq hqp
    have hnp : ¬ (N - q).Prime := fun hp => h q hq ⟨hqp, hp⟩
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hsq, hdvd⟩ := (not_prime_iff_exists_wheel (by omega)).mp hnp
    exact ⟨r, hr, hsq, ((Nat.modEq_iff_dvd' (by omega)).mpr hdvd).symm⟩
  · intro h q hq hs
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hsq, hmod⟩ := h q hq hs.1
    have hdvd : r ∣ N - q := (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd' (by omega)).mp (Eq.symm hmod)
    exact (not_prime_iff_exists_wheel (by omega)).mpr ⟨r, hr, hsq, hdvd⟩ hs.2

note.text: Closes the loop between the record game and the covering theory. With every prime up to √N allowed as a striker the statement is exact; the records choose residues for about 90 small moduli by design and leave the large primes to luck.

nodes.title: A generator for A025018, proved correct, that runs forever exactly if Goldbach holds
nodes.gist: A program that lists the record holders of the least Goldbach summand (OEIS A025018, with the summands in A025019), proved correct for every bound: what it lists below X is exactly the numbers that beat every smaller even number. It never stops exactly if Goldbach's conjecture is true.
nodes.detail: It is a sieve of translates of the primes. Take the primes 2, 3, 5, … in order as strikers; striker q strikes the numbers q + p for p prime. The front is the smallest even number from 4 not yet struck. If the next striker hits the front, the front is a term and q its value; if it misses (front − q composite) the front waits, which is why the summands skip primes (7 is followed by 19). mem_records and records_sorted hold for every X, and the kernel runs the program to 2^20 for the first 21 terms. exists_isFront shows the front always exists, and goldbach_iff_records_unbounded says the sequence is infinite exactly if every even number from 4 on is a sum of two primes.

nodes.title: Cover depth D(n): how far a set of moduli can strike the primes
nodes.gist: Give each modulus in a list one residue class. The vector strikes an odd prime q if q lies in the class of some modulus, and then every N in those classes has r dividing N − q. The depth of the list is the first odd prime that no vector strikes together with all smaller odd primes.
nodes.detail: IsDepth mods D says some vector strikes every odd prime below D and none strikes every odd prime up to D. For the first n odd primes this is the research session's function D(n). A depth-first search ("which modulus strikes the least unstruck prime?") decides the question and is proved correct (search_iff). The depth is unique, it is an odd prime, and a new modulus always raises it. A complete cover of the kind used in the 200-digit records is a lower bound for the depth of the primes it uses (coversBelow_of_complete_cover).
meta: CoverDepth.IsDepth.unique, CoverDepth.IsDepth.prime, CoverDepth.IsDepth.lt_cons, CoverDepth.CoversBelow, CoverDepth.CoversList, CoverDepth.coversBelow_of_complete_cover
nodes.source:
/-- `D` is the cover depth of `mods`: every odd prime below `D` can be struck by one vector,
and no vector strikes every odd prime up to `D`. -/
def IsDepth (mods : List ℕ) (D : ℕ) : Prop :=
  CoversBelow mods D ∧ ¬ CoversBelow mods (D + 1)

nodes.title: What the depth says about g(N): an upper bound, Goldbach by covering, a lower bound
nodes.gist: The least summand of an even N is at most the depth of the odd primes up to √N, because N's own residues strike every prime below it. Conversely, by Dirichlet's theorem, arbitrarily large even numbers have least summand at least the depth.

nodes.title: Counting complete covers: g0(x, Q) and its exact formula
nodes.gist: The number of class vectors modulo the odd primes up to x that cover every odd prime below Q is called g0(x, Q). Lean proves an exact inclusion–exclusion formula for it, that it can only fall as rows are added, and that it is positive exactly when Q is at most the cover depth.
nodes.detail: coverCount divided by the product of the moduli equals the sum, over sets T of rows left uncovered, of (−1)^|T| times the product over moduli r of (1 − ν_r(T)/r), where ν_r(T) is the number of classes modulo r that the rows of T occupy. With no rows the count is the product of the moduli (g0(x, 0) = e^θ(x)). isDepth_iff_coverCount says the depth is where the count reaches zero. Nothing about the size of the count is claimed beyond that.

/-- **The number of complete covers, by inclusion–exclusion** over the sets `T` of rows left
uncovered. (The subtraction is that of natural numbers; `ν_r(T) ≤ r` for a positive modulus.) -/
theorem coverCount_eq_sum (mods rows : Finset ℕ) :
    (coverCount mods rows : ℤ) =
      ∑ T ∈ rows.powerset, (-1) ^ #T * ∏ r ∈ mods, ((r - nu r T : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
  have h := inclusion_exclusion_card_inf_compl rows
    fun q => ({a : ClassVector mods | ¬ Covers a q} : Finset (ClassVector mods))
  have h1 : (rows.inf fun q =>
      ({a : ClassVector mods | ¬ Covers a q} : Finset (ClassVector mods))ᶜ) =
      ({a : ClassVector mods | ∀ q ∈ rows, Covers a q} : Finset (ClassVector mods)) := by
    ext a; simp [Finset.mem_inf]
  have h2 : ∀ T : Finset ℕ, (T.inf fun q =>
      ({a : ClassVector mods | ¬ Covers a q} : Finset (ClassVector mods))) =
      ({a : ClassVector mods | ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ Covers a q} : Finset (ClassVector mods)) := by
    intro T; ext a; simp [Finset.mem_inf]
  rw [h1] at h
  unfold cover

nodes.title: The first proved lower bounds for the number of covers
nodes.gist: If some vector on the odd primes up to x′ covers every odd prime below Q, the number of covers on the primes up to x is at least the product of the odd primes in (x′, x]: ln g0(x, Q) ≥ θ(x) − θ(x′). Every certified cover therefore bounds g0 for all larger prime sets.
nodes.detail: A cover on a subset of the moduli stays a cover whatever classes the other moduli take. Applied to the certified covers, from (x′, Q) = (97, 1,471) up to (9,973, 614,101). In the range of the covering bound (Q = c·y ln y for c below 1.349) it needs no data: the number of complete covers on the primes up to y is then at least e^((1 − cκ − ε)y) to leading order, with κ = 2C₂e^−γ. Exact small cases are checked too: for nine moduli g0(29, 181) is positive and g0(29, 182) is zero, and for 3, 5, 7 exactly one vector covers every odd prime below 19.

/-- **`ln g0(x, Q) ≥ θ(x) - θ(x')`** as soon as the odd primes up to `x'` can cover the odd
primes below `Q`: the product of the odd primes in `(x', x]` is at most `g0(x, Q)`. -/
theorem prod_le_g0 {x' x Q : ℕ} (h : x' ≤ x) (hpos : 0 < g0 x' Q) :
    ∏ r ∈ rowsBelow (x + 1) \ rowsBelow (x' + 1), r ≤ g0 x Q :=
  (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ hpos).trans (g0_mul_prod_le h Q)

nodes.title: Two rows in one class: the pair weight has mean exactly 6s/(s − 1)
nodes.gist: The research session's derivation of the law for the number of covers starts from pairs of rows q, q + d in one class of a modulus s. Lean proves its first exact step: averaged over the differences d = 6sj, the correction to independence (the pair weight, times the Hardy–Littlewood density of prime pairs) has mean exactly 6s/(s − 1).
nodes.detail: Each smaller modulus t draws its class among the t − 1 nonzero ones, and the two rows occupy one class if t divides d and two otherwise. Against independence the pair weight of t is (t − 1)/(t − 2) if t divides d and 1 − 1/(t − 2)² if not (at t = 3: 2 or 0). Together with the Hardy–Littlewood factor of t, the local factors cancel exactly for every prime t from 5, and the Chinese remainder theorem for sums gives the mean for every truncation of the products, so nothing about convergence is needed. The next step, the second-order term of the average of singular series, rests on the Hardy–Littlewood conjecture and is not touched.
nodes.source:
/-- **The mean of the pair weight is exactly `6 s/(s - 1)`.** Let `s ≥ 5` be prime, `B` a finite
set of primes `≥ 5` other than `s`, and `A ⊆ B`. The pair weights of the moduli `3` and `A`, times
the Hardy–Littlewood factors of `2`, `3`, `s` and `B`, summed over the differences `d = 6 s j`
with `j` in one period `∏ B`, give `6 s/(s - 1)` per term. -/
theorem sum_pair_weight {s : ℕ} (hs : s.Prime) (hs5 : 5 ≤ s) (A B : Finset ℕ) (hAB : A ⊆ B)
    (hB : ∀ t ∈ B, t.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ t ∧ t ≠ s) :
    ∑ j ∈ range (∏ t ∈ B, t),
        (rho 3 (6 * s * j) * ∏ t ∈ A, rho t (6 * s * j)) *
          (sigma 2 (6 * s * j) * sigma 3 (6 * s * j) * sigma s (6 * s * j) *
            ∏ t ∈ B, sigma t (6 * s * j)) =
      6 * (s : ℚ) / ((s : ℚ) - 1) * ∏ t ∈ B, (t : ℚ) := by
  classical
  -- the weight of a prime of `B`
  set w : ℕ → ℕ → ℚ := fun t j =>
    (if t ∈ A then rho t (6 * s * j) else 1) * sigma t (6 * s * j) with hwdef
  have hcop : ∀ t ∈ B, Nat.Coprime t (6 * s) := fun t ht => by
    obtain ⟨htp, ht
...

nodes.title: The pair weight in product form: its partial sums never exceed the mean
nodes.gist: The pair weight is a product over the primes dividing j, its partial sums are a finite sum with no cancellation, and they never exceed the mean: the sum of W(j) for j up to m is at most a·m for every m. As a by-product, the twin-prime constant C₂ is at least 1/2.
nodes.detail: W(j) = a·c·∏(1 + u_t) over the primes t dividing j, with u_t = 2/(t − 3) for the moduli that carry a pair weight and 1/(t − 2) for the others. The partial sums are a·c·∑ u(D)·⌊m/d(D)⌋ over subsets D of the primes, and the shortfall a·m minus the sum is a sum of nonnegative terms. This is what lets the research session compute the spread of rows within a class without cancellation. The limit profile of the spread, the price equation and the constant 1.1275 (withdrawn by the research session on 25 Nov) are heuristic and are not formalised.
nodes.source:
/-- **The partial sums never exceed the mean**: `∑_{j ≤ m} W(j) ≤ 6 s/(s - 1) · m` for every
`m`. -/
theorem sum_Ioc_pairWeight_le {s : ℕ} (hs : s.Prime) (hs5 : 5 ≤ s) (A B : Finset ℕ) (hAB : A ⊆ B)
    (hB : ∀ t ∈ B, t.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ t ∧ t ≠ s) (m : ℕ) :
    ∑ j ∈ Ioc 0 m, pairWeight s A B j ≤ 6 * (s : ℚ) / ((s : ℚ) - 1) * m := by
  have hdef := pairWeight_defect hs hs5 A B hAB hB m
  have hs2 : (2 : ℚ) ≤ s := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 2 ≤ s)
  have ha : 0 ≤ 6 * (s : ℚ) / ((s : ℚ) - 1) := div_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)
  have hcn : 0 ≤ ∏ t ∈ B, w0 A t :=
    prod_nonneg fun t ht => w0_nonneg A (by have := (hB t ht).2.1; omega)
  have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ D ∈ B.powerset, (∏ t ∈ D, uw A t) *
      ((m : ℚ) / (∏ t ∈ D, (t : ℚ)) - ((m / ∏ t ∈ D, t : ℕ) : ℚ)) := by
    refine sum_nonneg fun D hD => mul_nonneg ?_ ?_
    · exact prod_nonneg fun t ht =>
        uw_nonneg A (by have := (hB t (mem_powerset.1 hD ht)).2.1; omega)
    · have h := Nat.cast_div_le (α := ℚ) (m := m) (n := ∏ t ∈ D, t
...

nodes.title: The covering bound in depth form: covers exist up to 1.349 · y ln y
nodes.gist: For every c below e^γ/(2C₂) = 1.349 and all large y there are classes modulo the odd primes up to y such that every odd prime below c·y·ln y lies in one of them. In depth language: the cover depth of the odd primes up to y is at least c·y·ln y.
nodes.detail: This is the cover from which the asymptotic bound on g(N) is built (the layered cover of Cap/Layers.lean and Mertens' third theorem), stated so that it can be read as a lower bound for D(n) and for the count of covers. It needs no hypothesis. Combined with the count, it says the number of complete covers is positive, indeed exponentially large, in that range.
nodes.source:
/-- **The depth form, with the sharp constant and no hypothesis.** For every `c > 0` with
`c · 2 C₂ e^{-γ} < 1`, that is `c < e^γ / (2 C₂) = 1.349…`, and every large `y`, there are
classes modulo the odd primes up to `y` such that every odd prime below `⌊c y ln y⌋` lies in one
of them: the cover depth of the odd primes up to `y` is at least `c y ln y`. -/
theorem eventually_exists_classes_of_mul_lt_one {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c)
    (hc : c * (2 * twinPrimeConstant * Real.exp (-Real.eulerMascheroniConstant)) < 1) :
    ∀ᶠ y : ℕ in atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q ≠ 2 → q < ⌊c * y * Real.log y⌋₊ →
      ∃ r : ℕ, (r.Prime ∧ r ≠ 2 ∧ r ≤ y) ∧ q ≡ a r [MOD r] := by
  obtain ⟨κ', hκ'0, hcκ', hM'⟩ := exists_mertensUpper_pos mertensThird hc
  exact eventually_exists_classes_of_mertensUpper_nat hκ'0 hM' hc0 hcκ'

note.text: The proved lower bound D(n) ≳ 1.349·p_n ln p_n, against which the certified covers of the previous boxes sit 3.5 to 5 times higher. Superseded on 25 Nov: formally in the order ln X·(ln ln X)²/(150000 (ln ln ln X)²) by the box ‘The order of the covering bound in the kernel’.

nodes.title: Finding a covering vector is as hard as satisfiability, for arbitrary rows
nodes.gist: From a Boolean formula Lean builds prime moduli and rows so that the formula is satisfiable exactly when some residue vector covers every row, and exactly when some N does. So no method that treats the rows as arbitrary data can find covers quickly unless every problem in NP is easy.
nodes.detail: A formula with n variables and m clauses becomes n prime moduli and m(n + 1) rows. Variable i gets a prime larger than every residue used. Clause j gets n + 1 rows, each showing the prime of variable i the residue 1 if the clause contains the variable, 0 if it contains its negation, and otherwise a private dummy value. A satisfying assignment is a vector with classes 0 and 1. Conversely a clause has n + 1 rows with different dummies and only n variables, so one of its rows is covered through a literal. The depth-first search of the cover depth, run on these rows, decides the formula.
nodes.source:
/-- The same with a number in place of the residue vector: the formula is satisfiable exactly
when some `N` is congruent to every row modulo one of the moduli (every `N - q` has one of the
moduli as a factor). -/
theorem sat_iff_exists_number (φ : List (List Literal)) (n : ℕ)
    (hvars : ∀ C ∈ φ, ∀ l ∈ C, l.1 < n)
    (hcons : ∀ C ∈ φ, ∀ i, ¬ ((i, true) ∈ C ∧ (i, false) ∈ C)) :
    (∃ τ, Satisfies τ φ) ↔ ∃ N, ∀ q ∈ rows φ n, ∃ r ∈ mods φ n, q ≡ N [MOD r] := by
  rw [sat_iff_coversList φ n hvars hcons]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
    obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := Nat.chineseRemainderOfList (fun i => a (bigPrime (bound φ n) i))
      (bigPrime (bound φ n)) (List.range n) (coprime_bigPrime _ n)
    refine ⟨N, fun q hq => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hmod⟩ := ha q hq
    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hr
    exact ⟨_, hr, hmod.trans (hN i hi).symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨N, hN⟩
    exact ⟨fun _ => N, hN⟩

note.text: With the black-box theorem this narrows the field: only a method that uses the fact that the rows are the primes below the target could beat the present search. For that special case nothing is proved, and nothing is known either way.

nodes.title: A prime sieve on bitmasks that the kernel can run
nodes.gist: To prove a statement about every even number in a range of millions, the kernel sieves whole intervals at once with big-number operations on bitmasks, and the sieve is proved sound: a digit still set means the number is prime. A chain of interval statements then covers a whole range.
nodes.detail: segSieve clears the multiples of each prime from a window of ones; specCheck tests that every N of an interval divisible by m has a summand q ≤ G in the union of shifted prime masks; holds_of_segCheck turns the Boolean test into the statement. A chain of consecutive intervals (isChain, summand_of_chain) carries the statement over the union, and a table plus such a chain gives the complete list of record holders below X (isRecordHolder_of_mem, mem_of_isRecordHolder) or shows that no multiple of m enters the ten largest summands (notAmongTen_of_chain).

nodes.source:
/-- **Soundness of the segment test.** If `ds` holds every prime below `D` and the `qs` are
prime, a successful test proves every statement of the list. -/
theorem holds_of_segCheck {a L D : ℕ} {ds qs : List ℕ} {specs : List (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)}
    (hds : ∀ p, p.Prime → p < D → p ∈ ds) (hqs : ∀ q ∈ qs, q.Prime)
    (h : segCheck a L D ds qs specs = true) : ∀ s ∈ specs, Holds s := by
  simp only [segCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨ha, hD⟩, hr⟩, hall⟩ := h
  intro s hs N hA hB hm
  have hs' := List.all_eq_true.mp hall s hs
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hqG, hqj, hS⟩ := specCheck_sound hs' hA hB hm
  have hprime := prime_of_testBit_segSieve hr hds hD ha hS
  have ha1 : a ≤ s.1 := by
    simp only [specCheck, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at hs'
    exact hs'.1.1.1.1
  have h6 : a + (N - a - q) = N - q := by omega
  rw [h6] at hprime
  exact ⟨q, hqG, hqs q hq, hprime⟩
